top_candidates.original_title: Show HN: I wrote an email app that accepts only one sender per inbox
top_candidates.generated_headline: The Architectural Blindspot of Single-Sender Inboxes
top_candidates.summary: While radical email gating concepts like single-sender limits capture attention for reducing noise, the community highlights a fatal technical flaw: enterprise fragmentation and shifting corporate domains (such as rebrandings or multi-departmental sending addresses) mean hard-locking an inbox to a single sender inevitably causes critical messages to be silently dropped. Quote: If the 'Citibank inbox' just takes the first address that Citi happens to use and auto rejects all future others, user will lose critical emails without even knowing.

top_candidates.original_title: Why do LLM pelicans look like this?
top_candidates.generated_headline: The Mode Collapse of AI Generation
top_candidates.summary: When models produce generic or repetitive outputs, it is often a symptom of mode collapse during post-training rather than a failure of user prompting or a fundamental limitation of the underlying architecture. Quote: All current post-trained LLMs are mode-collapsed compared to the post-training set distribution, and this doesn't get nearly enough attention from the labs and independent researchers.
